findings.evidence: Proof step 1.2 is fragmented into five rows, of which only the first carries the number "1.2". Verified at 1:1 and re-cropped at 2x (capture y approximately 35400-35900): the numbered row ends at "[L5] and [L6] identify the coproducts of free algebras", and then the display $P:=\coprod_iF^T(TA_i),\qquad Q:=\coprod_iF^T(A_i)$, the prose "with free algebras on the corresponding base coproducts. If $j_i$ and $k_i$ are their coproduct injections, define $\alpha,\beta:P\rightrightarrows Q$ by", the display $\alpha j_i=k_iT(a_i),\qquad \beta j_i=k_i\mu_{A_i}$, and the prose "By hypothesis this pair has a coequalizer $q:Q\to R$ in $\mathcal C^T$. The construction also applies to the empty family." each render as a separate UNNUMBERED row flush with the step box's left edge, outside the numbered column. The citation tag renders as literal bracket text "[L5, L6, construct]" at the end of that last row instead of as tag chips: step 1.1 on the same page shows a chip `L1`, step 2.1 shows `step 1.2` `L4`, step 3.1 shows `step 1.2` `step 2.1` `L4` `construct`, and step 1.2 alone shows none. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 both cite "step 1.2", so a reader following that reference lands on a two-line fragment that does not contain the construction of $P$, $Q$, $\alpha$ or $\beta$ it is being pointed at. Cause is in the source: lines 50-58 split step 1.2 into three paragraphs separated by blank-line `$$` blocks, and only the paragraph opening with "1.2 " is parsed as the step.
findings.repair: In items/prop-a-monadic-category-over-a-cocomplete-base-is-cocomplete-iff-it-has-coequalizers.md, join lines 50-58 into the single Markdown paragraph the step parser expects: delete the four blank lines so that step 1.2's prose, both `$$...$$` displays and the trailing `[L5, L6, construct]` tag sit on one line. This shape is already used and renders correctly across the corpus (for example items/thm-hadamard-three-lines.md and items/thm-hessian-characterises-convexity.md, and on this run outer-measure-and-the-caratheodory-extension-theorem and volumes-of-elementary-solids-and-solids-of-revolution): the step keeps its number and its tag chips, and each display still breaks onto its own centred line inside the step's own cell.

findings.evidence: Fact [F1] of "Stirling's factorial asymptotic holds up to a positive constant" renders its citation as RAW Markdown: the reader sees "([The power series for log(1+x) on (-1,1], including the Abel endpoint](/item/thm-log-one-plus-x-power-series))", with visible square brackets, a visible parenthesised route, and no clickable link - unlike every other fact on all 26 pages, which render as an underlined title. The app expands the source wikilink `[[thm-log-one-plus-x-power-series]]` into `[<title>](/item/<id>)`, and that title contains a bare `]` in "(-1,1]" outside math, which closes the link label early and leaves the remainder as literal text. A scan of every wikilink target reachable from the 26 pages found this is the only target in the run whose title carries `[` or `]` outside `$...$`; targets whose brackets sit inside math, such as "$[G:H]$" on the-galois-correspondence and "$\mathbb R[x]/(x^2+1)$" on the-identity-theorem-and-the-open-mapping-theorem, render as proper links.
findings.repair: In items/lem-stirling-formula-up-to-a-positive-constant.md line 33, give the wikilink an explicit bracket-free display text using the aliased form SCHEMA.md section 4 already specifies: replace `([[thm-log-one-plus-x-power-series]])` with `([[thm-log-one-plus-x-power-series|The power series for log(1+x), including the Abel endpoint]])`. The target id, the `deps` entry, the dependency graph and the fact's own statement are untouched - [F1] already states the domain exactly as "For $-1<x\le1$" - and the only change is the label the link displays, which becomes a working citation instead of raw markup. Keep the label free of `[` and `]`: tools/facts-block.mjs matches wikilinks with `/\[\[([^\]|]+)(?:\|[^\]]*)?\]\]/`, so a bracket inside the label would break the repo's own link extraction too.

summary: Rejected, but this is a much smaller rejection than the previous one. All 26 manifest captures were reviewed at 1:1 by slicing each full-page PNG into 1900px bands over the content column (376 bands in all), with 2x-6x nearest-neighbour re-crops wherever a defect was suspected, cross-checked against the source items. The app-side regression that produced eight blocked findings last time is FIXED at app HEAD 2f098c5c: display fractions whose denominator carries a script now paint correctly (verified at 6x on prop-two-classical-counterexamples-in-polar-coordinates, and again on the Bohr-Mollerup $G_n(x)$, Stirling's ratio and $1/f'(g(w))$); `\ne` and `\notin` render as proper crossed glyphs on every page including item titles; a subscript on a norm delimiter is again a small lowered subscript, so $\lVert f'(t)\rVert_2=1$ reads correctly; paired `_2^2` scripts stack instead of overlapping; Markdown tables have cell padding, so the S3 correspondence table separates $\langle r\rangle=A_3$ from $\mathbb Q(\omega)$ and the order-360 table no longer manufactures $\mathbb Z/5\mathbb Z$ out of two columns; and no inline math was found broken mid-atom. Tau's two source repairs are also verified in place: the transitive-subgroups-of-$S_4$ table now parses as a four-column table with all five rows, and the 3x3 spherical Jacobian renders whole inside its own delimiters. Three publication-blocking findings remain, all proof-parsing, all with clean in-place repairs. Two are the same defect on monadicity-and-becks-theorem, where a proof step written across several Markdown blocks loses its number, its tag chips and its indentation: the step's citation tag prints as literal bracket text and its displays and continuing prose become unnumbered rows, while later steps still cite it by number (S-001, S-002; a scan of every proof step on all 26 pages found exactly these two). The third is a wikilink whose target title carries a bare `]` outside math, so the generated Markdown link breaks and Fact [F1] of the Stirling lemma shows raw brackets and a raw /item/ route (S-003; the only such target in the run). Not filed, and noted only: the Logical flowchart box is empty on the A pages whose items carry no landmarks while populating correctly on frattini, sums-of-two-squares and monadicity-examples, which is curation, not a rendering fault, and is outside the three finding types; the regular-surfaces summary prints backticked page slugs as inline code, which renders exactly as authored; fs-one-existing-iterated-integral-guarantees-multiple-riemann-integrability lists [F2] before [F1] in its own source, so the renderer is faithful and the ordering is an authoring question for the judges; and a display written inline inside a step sometimes leaves its sentence's closing period or comma alone on the next line, which is cosmetic and changes no content. No TikZ or tikz-cd defects were found: the category-theory arrow diagrams and pullback square, the companion, Smith-form and Jacobian matrices, and the group-of-order-27 matrix all render correctly.
